description: FILED s513 (Fable, 2026-10-10) from the production-readiness review (docs/production-readiness-review-s513.md section 4f): nothing measures PCL's behaviour over TIME.  Every population runs a program to its end in seconds; a production process runs for hours.  Unmeasured today: (1) RSS over time (a steady climb = a leak: boxes kept alive by a cache, streams not closed until GC because DESTROY runs at collection -- docs/not-supported.md 'DESTROY called by garbage collector'); (2) open file descriptors over time (`ls /proc/PID/fd | wc -l` sampled; a handle opened in a loop and dropped is closed by the GC's finalizer, not at scope exit -- how many fds does a loop of 10k open/drop iterations hold at its peak?); (3) GC pause distribution (SBCL's gen-GC under a steady allocation rate: max pause, p99); (4) signal delivery during a long run (SIGTERM/SIGHUP handlers installed with %SIG fire within one iteration); (5) behaviour at memory pressure (a MemoryMax scope at 512 MB: does the process die tidily with perl's shape, 'Out of memory!', or hang?).  SHAPE: tools/soak.pl PROG.pl --minutes N --sample 10 writes a TSV (t, rss_kb, fds, gc_pauses_ms_max) and a summary line; a soak CORPUS of three programs under everyday/soak/ (a line-oriented log processor reading a FIFO; a hash-keyed counter with periodic flush and reopen; an object-churn loop with Moo objects carrying a DESTROY) each with its perl twin; the baseline is the per-program summary, rows leave by edit.  Run it OUTSIDE the gate (minutes to an hour), on a quiet box, through heavy.sh; record the first run in docs/production-readiness-review-s513.md section 4f.  A leak found here is filed as its own task with the sample curve.  One agent session for the tool + corpus + first run.
subject: SOAK TEST before any production wording: a server-shaped program (accept / read / regex / hash update / print / close, in a loop) run for an hour under PCL -- RSS over time, open file descriptors, GC pauses, a DESTROY-less resource leak made visible; tools/soak.pl + a baseline row
